translations.text: And from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar.
And from Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran.
These are the chosen men of their camps, the representatives of their tribes. According to their clans, they are the leaders of Israel.
Moses and Aaron took these men who had been named individually.

And the descendants of Simeon, according to their clans, their families, and their ancestral households, counted by name and individually: every male twenty years old and over, everyone able to go out with the army;
Those counted from the tribe of Dan were 72,700.
Only you shall not count the tribe of Levi or include their number among the Israelites.
When the tent is being moved, the Levites shall take it down; when the tent is to remain in place, they shall set it up. Anyone from another clan who joins them in this work shall die.
The Israelites shall camp, each man with his companion and each man with his division, according to their armies.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
With his army, those counted were 54,400.
With his army, those counted were 57,400.
All those counted in the camp of Judah, with their armies, were 186,400. They shall set out first.
With his army, those counted were 45,750.
All those counted in the camp of Ephraim, with their armies, were 108,100. They shall set out third.
This was the number of the Israelites according to their ancestral households. The total number in their camps, with their armies, was 603,550.
These are the names of Aaron's sons: Nadab his firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

Look, I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the Israelites. As their ransom, the Levites shall belong to me (said the Lord). For on that day I consecrated all the firstborn in the land of Egypt. Every firstborn in Israel, from human beings to livestock, belongs to me, for I am the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai and said to him:
And the sons of Merari, according to their families, were Mahli and Mushi;
And of Kohath there was one clan of Amram, one clan of Izhar, one clan of Hebron, and one clan of Uzziel.
The total number of the Levites whom Moses and Aaron counted at the Lord's command, according to their families—all their males one month old and over—was 22,000.
And as the ransom for those 273 firstborn Israelites who exceeded the number of the Levites.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
This is the work of the descendants of Kohath in the tent of testimony: the most holy things.
Aaron and his sons shall enter when the camp sets out. They shall take down the screening curtain and cover the ark of testimony with it.
They shall put it and all its utensils inside a covering of [?] skin and place it on its carrying frame.

They shall put in it all the utensils they use in their work: the censers, the forks, the bowls, their covers, and all the utensils of the altar. They shall put a covering of [?] skin over it and set it on its carrying frame. They shall take a purple cloth and cover the basin and its stand, put them inside a covering of [?] skin, and set them on their carrying frame.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
Do this for them so that they may live and not die when they enter the Holy of Holies: Aaron and his sons shall go in and assign each of them his load.
Take a census of the descendants of Gershon, by their ancestral households and their clans.
Count all those from twenty-five years old up to fifty years old who enter to perform work in the tent of testimony.
All those from twenty-five years old up to fifty years old who enter to perform the work of the tent of testimony.
Their number, by their clans and their ancestral households, was 3,200.
All those from twenty-five years old up to fifty years old who enter the service to perform the work of carrying the things of the tent of testimony.
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If any man's wife sins and is unfaithful to him,

that man shall bring his wife to the priest and bring her offering on her behalf: a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He shall not pour oil over it or put frankincense on it, because it is an offering under the law of jealousy, a memorial offering that brings sin to remembrance.
But if you have been unfaithful to your husband and defiled yourself, and someone other than your husband has slept with you,
the accursed water of the ordeal shall enter her belly.

He shall consecrate himself to the Lord for all the days of his vow and bring a year-old lamb as a guilt offering. The previous days shall not be counted for him, because he has defiled the vow concerning his head.
On the day when Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed and consecrated it and all its furnishings, as well as the altar and all its utensils; he anointed and consecrated them.
The Lord said to Moses, “One leader each day shall bring his offering, each leader on his appointed day, for the dedication of the altar.”

He brought his offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one bull from among the cattle, one ram, and one year-old lamb for a burnt offering.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And for a peace offering, two cattle, five rams, five goats, and five year-old ewe lambs. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And for a peace offering, two cattle, five rams, five goats, and five year-old ewe lambs. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Reuel.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one bull from among the cattle, one ram, and one year-old lamb for a burnt offering.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
On the ninth day, Abidan son of Gideoni, the leader of the descendants of Benjamin, brought his offering.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
On the tenth day, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai, the leader of the descendants of Dan, brought his offering.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
For the peace offering, two calves, five sheep, five goats, and five ewes, each a year old. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.
Take the Levites from among the Israelites and purify them.
This is the rule concerning the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward, they shall enter to perform their work, the service of the tent of meeting.
His brother shall serve in the tent of meeting and keep their charge, but they shall not perform the labor. This is how you shall deal with the Levites concerning their respective duties.
Some men came who were themselves unclean and could not observe the Passover that day. They came before Moses and Aaron that same day.
Moses said to them, “Wait here, and I will hear what the Lord commands concerning you.”
Tell the Israelites and say to them, “If anyone is unclean through a human corpse or is in a distant land, whether among you or among your descendants, they shall observe the Lord’s Passover.
They shall observe it in the second month, on the fourteenth day of the waxing moon, toward evening. They shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

If a foreigner comes to you in your land, he shall observe the Lord’s Passover. They shall observe it according to the law of the Passover and its commands. There shall be one law for you, both for the foreigner and for the native-born.”
When the cloud remained from evening until morning and lifted at dawn, they would set out during the day.
If the cloud remained for a long time, overshadowing it for a month, the Israelites would remain encamped and would not set out.

You shall sound their signal a second time, and the camps of those encamped toward the south shall set out. You shall sound their signal a third time, and the camps of those encamped toward the west shall set out. You shall sound their signal a fourth time, and the camps of those encamped toward the north shall set out. When they are to set out, you shall sound a signal.
The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets. This shall be an everlasting ordinance for you throughout your generations.
In the second month of the second year, on the fifth day of the waning moon, the cloud lifted from the tent of meeting.
The Israelites set out on their journey from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud stopped in the wilderness of Paran.
The descendants of Kohath shall set out carrying the holy things, and they shall set up the tent before their arrival.
Over the army of the tribe of Benjamin was Abidan son of Gideoni.
But now we are dried up; we have nothing else to look at except manna.

You shall say to the people, “Purify yourselves for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat. For you wept before the Lord, saying, ‘Who will give us meat to eat? We were better off in the land of Egypt.’ The Lord will give you meat to eat, and you shall eat meat.”

The Lord came down in the cloud and spoke to him. He took some of the spirit that was upon him and placed it upon the seventy elders. When the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, but they did not do so again.
I speak to him mouth to mouth, openly and not in hidden words, and he has seen the glory of the Lord. Why, then, were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?
Send men as scouts to inspect the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites to rule over: one man from each of their tribes and from their ancestral clans. You shall send their leaders.
From the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori.
From the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli.
The people who live in that land are strong, and its cities are very strongly fortified and large, and they have walls. We also saw the descendants of Anak there.
The whole assembly gathered together and cried out aloud, and the people wept all night.
They said to one another, “Let us appoint a ruler for ourselves and return to the land of Egypt.”
Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before the whole assembly of the Israelites.
If the Lord has chosen us, he will bring us into that land and give it to us—a land flowing with milk and honey.
The Lord said to Moses, “How long will this people reject me? How long will they refuse to believe in me, despite all the signs I have performed for them?”
Tell them, “As I live, says the Lord, I will certainly do to you in this wilderness just as you have spoken in my hearing.”
For Amalek and Canaan are there before you, and you will fall by the sword because you turned away and rejected the Lord. The Lord is not with you.
They boldly went up to the top of the mountain, but the ark of the Lord’s law and Moses did not move from the midst of the assembly.
When you offer a ram as an offering or a sacrifice, you shall make an offering of two tenths of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil.
And half a hin of wine for a drink offering, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
This is what you shall do for each bull, each ram, or each lamb from among the sheep or the goats.
According to the number you offer, you shall do this for each one, in proportion to their number.
Everyone who is native-born shall do this, and in this way bring his offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

If something has escaped the notice of the assembly, the whole assembly shall offer one unblemished bull from the herd as a sacrifice with a pleasing aroma to the Lord, together with its grain offering and its drink offering according to the law, and one male goat from the goats as a sin offering.
They stood against Moses, together with two hundred and fifty men from among the Israelites, leaders of the assembly, chosen for the council and men of renown.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
They fell on their faces and said, “Lord, God of every spirit and all flesh, if one man has sinned, will the Lord’s wrath come upon the whole assembly?”
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
Write Aaron’s name on Levi’s staff, for each tribe of their ancestral houses shall give one staff.

You and your sons with you shall guard your priesthood according to every law concerning the altar and what is inside the curtain, and perform the service that is the gift of your priesthood. Anyone from another family who enters shall die.

The Lord said to Aaron, “Look, I have given you charge of the first offerings brought to me, from everything the Israelites consecrate to me. I have given it to you until you [?], and after you to your sons, as an everlasting ordinance.”
Eat it in the most holy place. Every male shall eat it—you and your sons—for it is holy to you.
All the firstfruits of the grain from all their land, and everything they bring to the Lord, I have given to you. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat it.

The Levites shall perform this service of the tent of testimony, and they shall bear their sins. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout their generations, and they shall inherit no inheritance among the Israelites.
Tell them, “When you set aside some of the firstfruits, it shall be counted for the Levites as grain from the threshing floor and as wine from the winepress.”
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
They shall burn it in his presence. They shall burn its hide, its flesh, and its blood together with its dung.
Anyone who touches the dead body of any human being is unclean for seven days.
This is the law concerning a person who dies inside a house: everyone who enters that house and everyone who is inside the house is unclean for seven days.
For that unclean person they shall take some of the ashes of what they burned for purification, and mix fresh water with them in a vessel.
Israel took all those cities, and Israel lived in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon and throughout its territory.
Israel lived in all the cities of the Amorites.
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went, taking their divination equipment with them. They reached Balaam and told him Balak’s message.
When the donkey saw the angel of the Lord, she pressed against the wall and scraped Balaam’s foot. He struck her again.
The Lord opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you strike me? This is now the third time!”
The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, whom you have ridden from your youth until today, this very day? Have I ever been accustomed to treating you this way?” He said to her, “No.”
The angel of the Lord said to Balaam, “Go with these men, but take care to speak only the words I tell you.” Balaam went with Balak’s messengers.
When Balak heard that Balaam had come, he went out to meet him in the city of Moab on the border of the Arnon, at one end of their territory.
Balaam said to Balak, “Look, I have come to you. Now I can speak the word that God puts in my mouth, and I will take care to speak it.”
In the morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to the monument of Baal. From there he showed him a portion of the people.
Balak did as Balaam told him and offered a bull and a ram on the altar.
Balaam went to inquire of God, going straight ahead. God appeared to Balaam, and Balaam said to God, “I have prepared seven cattle, and they have offered a bull and a ram on the altar.”
He took him and led him around into the wilderness, to the summit of the hewn rock. He built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on the altar.
Look, I have come to bless him. I will bless, and it will not be reversed.
When Balaam saw that it was good in the Lord’s sight to bless Israel, he did not go, as he usually did, to seek divination before him. Instead, he turned his face toward the wilderness.
Balaam raised his eyes and saw Israel moving tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came upon him.
He spoke his saying and said, “Balaam son of Beor says; the man who sees clearly says:
How beautiful are your houses, Jacob, and your tents, Israel!
Now go home. I said I would honor you, but now the Lord has not given you honor.”
Edom will become his possession, and Esau, his enemy, will become his possession. Israel acted with strength.
After the plague, the Lord spoke to Moses and to Eleazar the priest and said to them:
The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These were leaders of the assembly; they were the ones who rose against Moses and Aaron in Korah’s assembly when they opposed the Lord.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and Korah. He and their assembly died when fire consumed the 250, and they became a warning sign.
The sons of Judah were Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
From Azen came the Azenite clan, and from Sad came the Sadite clan.
These were the people of Manasseh, and their number was 52,700.
The sons of Dan, according to their clans: from Shuham came the Shuhamite clan. These were the people of Dan according to their clans.
These shall inherit that land according to their allotted portions and according to the number of their names.
Their allotted portions shall come to them by lot, to those named according to the clans of their fathers.
They shall inherit from their allotted portions, receiving their inheritance among the many and the few.
Their number was 23,000, every male one month old and older. They were not counted with the Israelites, because no allotted portion was given to them among the Israelites.
This was the census taken by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who counted the Israelites on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho.
For the Lord had told them that they would certainly die in the wilderness. Not one of them remained except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
The daughters of Zelophehad have spoken rightly. Give them their allotted inheritance among their father’s brothers, and transfer their father’s allotted portion to them.

If his father has no brothers, give his inheritance to his nearest relative’s household within his clan, and he shall inherit it. This shall be a statute of my judgment for the Israelites, as the Lord commanded Moses.
See it, and then you too shall be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron was gathered on Mount Hor.
Let the Lord, the God of every soul and all flesh, appoint a man for this assembly,
who will go out and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the Lord’s assembly will not be like sheep without a shepherd.
Command the Israelites and say to them: Take care to bring me my offering, my gift, and my sacrifices of a pleasing aroma at my appointed festivals.
On the fifteenth day of that month there shall be a festival; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
You shall bring an offering to the Lord: two bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven lambs. They shall be one year old and without blemish.
You shall do this each day for seven days, a sacrificial offering of a pleasing aroma to the Lord, in addition to the regular sacrifice. You shall also make the drink offering.
You shall offer a sacrifice of a pleasing aroma to the Lord: one bull from the herd, one ram, and seven lambs, each one year old and without blemish.
On the second day: twelve bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs, each one year old and without blemish.
And one young goat from among the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
On the third day: eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs, each one year old and without blemish.
And one young goat from among the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
And one young goat from among the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
And one young goat from among the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
And one young goat from among the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
And one young goat from among the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
But if he does this to her after the day on which he heard it, he will bear the guilt.
And they fought against Midian, as the Lord had commanded Moses, and killed all their males.
They also killed the kings of Midian along with the others they killed: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword in that slaughter.
And Moses said to them, “Why have you kept all the women alive?”
And the human beings of the female sex who had not known a man numbered 32,000 persons in all.
And the tribute for the Lord from the sheep was 775.
And Moses gave the tribute for the Lord, which they had set aside for the Lord, to Eleazar the priest, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And all those appointed over the army, the army commanders and officers, came to Moses.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest took that gold from the army commanders and officers and brought it into the tent of testimony as a memorial for the Israelites.

“These men who came out of Egypt, those among them who were twenty years old and older and knew good and evil, shall not see the land that the Lord swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they did not follow me.”
And the Lord’s anger burned against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until all that generation who did evil before the Lord had perished.
“But we will go fully equipped with our weapons ahead of the Israelites until we bring them to their place. Our possessions will remain in fortified towns because of the inhabitants of the land.”
And Moses said to them, “If you do as you say and go with your weapons before the Lord into battle,
“But we will all go, equipped with our weapons, arrayed before the Lord for battle, as you say to us, my lord.”
And Moses appointed over them Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel.

“But if they do not cross over with you, equipped with their weapons, into battle before the Lord, bring their possessions, their wives, and their livestock across ahead of you into the land of Canaan.”
“We will cross over with our weapons before the Lord into the land of Canaan, and give us our allotted portion on the other side of the Jordan.”
And Baal-meon and their fortifications and Sibmah; and they gave names to the towns they had built.
And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages, and named them Nobah after himself.
And there were Egyptians burying their dead, all those whom the Lord had killed, every firstborn in the land of Egypt. The Lord also took vengeance on their gods.
And they set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
And they set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
And they set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
And they set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, opposite Nebo.

But if you do not destroy the inhabitants of that land before you, those whom you leave alive will become thorns in your eyes and prickles in your sides, and they will oppose you in the land where you live.
From mountain to mountain, the boundary shall be marked out for you, reaching as far as Hamath, and its endpoint shall be the border of Zedad.
The boundary shall descend to the Jordan, and its endpoint shall be the Salt Sea. This shall be your land, with its boundaries all around it.
Take one representative from each tribe to allot that land to you as your inheritance.
From the tribe of the descendants of Asher, the representative shall be Ahihud son of Shelomi.
Those cities shall be places of refuge for you from the avenger of blood, so that the killer does not die before standing before the assembly and being tried.
If he strikes someone with a stone or drops it on him from his hand, and that person dies, he is a murderer. The one who killed shall surely be put to death.
The avenger of blood himself shall kill him.
Or if he kills someone unknowingly with any stone that causes his death, without being his enemy or intending to harm him;
The assembly shall judge between the killer and the avenger of blood according to this law.
This is what the Lord commanded the daughters of Zelophehad, saying: “Let them marry whoever pleases them, but let them marry within the tribe of their fathers.”
